title: Seminar · Hold out whole batches and their related questions
question: If the same question appears with the tray colors renamed and the arrival order unchanged, what would determine its split?
answer: Its source batch and generation history. A renamed copy of the amber instance stays with amber. The program detects overlap only when the family IDs are assigned correctly.

title: Seminar · Run two methods on the same four cards
question: Why keep the A2 question when both methods return the same number?
answer: It is an unchanged-outcome control. Execution can show that the last tray was already waiting. Lookup reproduces the same number by repeating history. The numerical match alone cannot distinguish the two explanations.

title: Seminar · Separate the numeric result, the evidence and the scope decision
question: Suppose A1 reports 18 with all the expected IDs. Which checks would that answer pass?
answer: It passes scope and citation completeness, then fails the numerical check. Inspecting the trace would show where the answer departed from the process. Conversely, the lookup baseline gets A2’s number right while citing only the original historical record.

title: Independent task
question: Make a four-row audit ledger by running both methods. For each supported request record numerical correctness, citation completeness and the trace. For the unsupported request record whether the method abstained. Then inject two independent test faults into the execution outputs: remove the change-card citation from A1 and add one minute to J1’s final answer. Verify that your evaluator distinguishes them.

title: Module overview · Compare lookup and execution on matched interventions
question: What is this module about?
answer: Compare lookup and execution on matched interventions. Design a held-out comparison, score numerical answers separately from scope decisions and cited evidence, and identify a case that needs a reliability check.
